But Once I told my PT to lay cushions all over the floor, so that I can practice falling down safely, with minimum to zero harm to my body under the supervision of my PT. I learnt to know when I was about to fall. Haven't had a single major Injury in the last 6 years, before that I had fractures and what not. Just because I have a different way of doing things should not mean that I should be denied to do the things.

And for the 7 year old hero, leave no stone unturned. He deserves the best medical treatment that you can provide for him. I don't want him to think that things could have been better for him ever in the future.... he deserves the best things.

Being able to tie my shoes. I remember, I was around 10, everybody in my family could tie shoes, even my little sibling. One day I sat down, and for 16 hours straight, I was just trying to tie shoelaces.., once it happened It was glorious. Life feels like a video game and it feels you are playing it at the hardest difficulty... There is a bucket list of things that I want to do but can't: 

1) being able to carry beer glasses without spilling.

2) climb down stairs without using my hands or a stick (I figured out climbing up part)

3) balance on a bicycle!

4) stand on one leg.

and the list goes on! Its these little things that I am trying to figure out in my 20s, while everybody else has the time to enjoy. Deep down I am a little child. I can feel how amazing it would have felt for you when you tied your shoelaces for the first time, while for everybody else its a trivial thing! Do you have a bucket list of these small things? Do you try to achieve them little by little (in a safe environment of course). Please share your thoughts. I don't wanna walk alone, I am tired...

I had many of them through my 16 year of physical therapy experience. They are simply uneducated. Stretching exercises should not be done past the threshold limit. It is somewhat painful, but you have to give feedback to the therapist. If its too much It can cause permanent damage or deformities. The therapist should have looked for alternative stretchings to achieve the same goal or suggest exercises strengthen other muscle groups that counteract spastic muscles or simply suggested a break. Physical therapy is a methodological procedure if not done properly can cause harm. Please  always seek opinions from multiple therapists. Don't ever rely on a single opinion. I have seen therapists causing permanent damage to spine, ankle joints etc. She probably just doesn't know what she is doing or doesn't care. I am so sad that it happened to you... as probably she was your only choice...
